newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DSM hikes Q1 profits, upgrades H1 outlook.
newsitem.headline: DSM hikes Q1 profits, upgrades H1 outlook.

text.p: Dutch chemicals group DSM NV said on Tuesday first-quarter net profits rose nine percent in 1997 and upgraded its forecast for the first half.
DSM said first-quarter net earnings from ordinary operations rose to 223 million guilders from a year-earlier 216 million, helped by recovering margins and increased demand.
Total net profit was up from a year-earlier 205 million, when DSM booked a 10 million guilder extraordinary loss.

"There are no signs that the present favourable market conditions will change in a major way in the coming months. Based on this, we expect the results for the first half of 1997 to be higher than those for the first half of 1996," DSM said.
In February, DSM predicted half-year results would be broadly in line with the previous year's.
Chairman Simon de Bree said profit margins had on average almost recovered to the levels of the first quarter of 1996 as higher selling prices offset increases in raw materials.
"The upward trend in the selling prices of a number of important DSM products which had started in the second half of 1996 continued in the first quarter of 1997," DSM said.
It said higher margins on hydrocarbons and plastics had been partly neutralised by lower margins on fibre intermediates, melamine, elastomers and fertilizers.
Higher selling prices boosted turnover by five percent, while higher volumes accounted for a further seven percent increase and exchange rates three percent, DSM said.
It had benefited from a slight increase in European economic growth and faster-than-expected growth in the United States, while growth in Asia remained high.
However, it was too early to give a forecast for the full year, DSM said.
Analysts said the upturn in chemicals prices justified a rather more upbeat response.
"I would have liked the company to be more positive about the future," said Peter Schouten, analyst with MeesPierson.
"There were fears over chemical prices for the end of 1997 and they have gone away...polymer prices are on the way up and DSM is on course for a very strong second quarter."
"DSM is a little reluctant on its prospects," Kempen & Co's Peter Beijers said. "The underlying trend is positive and there is good volume growth."
At 223 million guilders, the ordinary net profit figure came in ahead of analysts' consensus forecast of 217 million.
Investors cheered the news, sending DSM shares 4.40 guilders or 2.21 percent higher to 194.20 by 0850 GMT on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange, which was generally around 0.6 percent firmer.
